I have resolved the issue where email messages crash when the domain name contains non-ASCII characters and the email encoding is set to a non-Unicode charset (such as `iso-8859-1`).

### Solution
1. **[django/core/mail/utils.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-mvbpnboi/django/core/mail/utils.py#L16)**: Updated `CachedDnsName.get_fqdn()` to convert `socket.getfqdn()` to punycode/IDNA ASCII via `.encode('idna').decode('ascii')`.
2. **[django/core/mail/message.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-mvbpnboi/django/core/mail/message.py#L260)**: Updated domain formatting for `make_msgid(domain=...)` to ensure `DNS_NAME` is converted to IDNA ASCII before creating the `Message-ID` header, even if `DNS_NAME` is patched or set to a non-ASCII string.
3. **[tests/mail/tests.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-mvbpnboi/tests/mail/tests.py#L409-L420)**: Added unit tests verifying `CachedDnsName` IDNA encoding and `Message-ID` creation when non-ASCII domain hostnames are used with `iso-8859-1` email encoding.
